title: Stygian feudalism
summary: Why the Hierarchy keeps a medieval order.

claims.text: Feudalism in the living world gave the Hierarchy a stable model: everyone knew their place, owing loyalty upward and expecting it from below, which strengthened Stygia as a bulwark against Oblivion.
The living have moved on, but Stygia resists modernizing, fearing that any change of government would leave it open to Spectral armies.
Fugitives are wraiths who crossed the Hierarchy and escaped: runaway thralls, thieves, members of banned guilds, black marketeers, outlaws, and fallen Hierarchs ruined by rivals.
They band into Circles for survival, with leadership that shifts often; some bands are known for daring stands against their hunters, others for savagery that frightens most wraiths.

title: The Dark Kingdom of Ivory
summary: The African realm of the dead.

claims.text: In the African Underworld the souls of animals exist beside human souls, beings calling themselves gods compete for power and worship, and the Shadowlands look ominously lush.
No way to make lasting matter from souls is known there, so Artifacts and relics are worth far more than elsewhere.
The Dark Kingdom of Ivory deals often with Stygia yet little true knowledge escapes it; even its name is an outsider's label, not what its own dead call it.

title: The Kingdom of Clay
summary: The Aboriginal realm of the dead beside Australia.

claims.text: Few Stygian wraiths know of the Kingdom of Clay, which lies in the Tempest beside the Shadowlands of Australia, where colonial wraiths cling to the days of British rule.
It is a kingdom with no king, free of the tyranny of Stygia's rulers, and named not for a rare substance but for the earth itself, a reminder of the bond between its Aboriginal dead and their land.

title: Lost Fetters
summary: What happens when a Fetter is destroyed.

claims.text: A Fetter destroyed in the living world, or a living Fetter who dies before resolution, is lost for good.

A wraith may pull a destroyed object across the Shroud as a relic, but it no longer ties the wraith to the living and gains no powers; abandoning a Fetter by choice is almost unheard of because of what it costs.
